title: Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking Transitions on a Quantum Processor
authors: Zhi-Yuan Wei, Christopher Fechisin, Yu-Xin Wang, Jeet Shah, Tsung-Cheng Lu, Cheng-Ju Lin, Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract: Mixed quantum states can exhibit unconventional forms of symmetry breaking without pure-state counterparts. A prominent example is strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB), which cannot be diagnosed by observables linear in the density matrix. Here, we experimentally resolve finite-size critical signatures of SW-SSB transitions on a superconducting quantum processor. We develop a measurement protocol that combines quantum measurements with classical processing based on the known dephasing channel to reconstruct nonlinear mixed-state correlators. Using only two measurement settings, the protocol reconstructs fidelity, Rényi-2, and linear correlators, as well as string observables. Applying this approach to matrix-product states subjected to power-law-correlated dephasing, we observe finite-size crossings and scaling collapses in nonlinear correlators, accompanied by decaying linear correlations. We further map the estimated SW-SSB transition points across initial-state and channel parameters. Measurements of linear and Rényi-2 string observables further reveal signatures of mixed-state symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases, with a nonlinear string-order crossover aligned with an independently estimated SW-SSB transition point. Our results establish a quantum-classical approach to probing SW-SSB critical behavior and mixed-state SPT order.
summary: This work experimentally investigates Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking (SW-SSB) transitions in mixed quantum states using a superconducting quantum processor. The authors introduce a novel quantum-classical measurement protocol to reconstruct nonlinear correlators, allowing them to observe finite-size critical scaling signatures. This establishes a powerful quantum-classical approach for diagnosing complex symmetry breaking and topological order in noisy quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of experimentally characterizing Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking (SW-SSB) transitions in mixed quantum states, which cannot be detected using simple linear observables.
main_result: The authors report the first experimental observation of finite-size critical scaling for SW-SSB transitions on a superconducting quantum processor, successfully mapping the transition points across various system parameters.
method: A quantum-classical measurement protocol is developed to reconstruct nonlinear mixed-state correlators (like fidelity and Rényi-2) using only two measurement settings, allowing for the diagnosis of non-linear critical behavior.
model_or_system: The study uses a superconducting quantum processor to simulate mixed states generated by applying a power-law-correlated dephasing channel to an initial Matrix-Product State (MPS).
key_observables: Fidelity correlator ($C_F$), Rényi-2 correlator ($C_{II}$), linear correlators ($C_I$), and string observables ($S_I, S_{II}$).
important_parameters: Dephasing strength ($p$), correlation exponent ($\alpha$), and an initial state parameter ($g$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the ability to map the transition points across a tunable parameter space and compares QPU results against exact finite-chain calculations.
figures_summary: Figures demonstrate finite-size scaling analysis for $C_{II}$ and $C_F$ across varying $g$ and $\alpha$, and show the distinct behavior of string order parameters ($S_I$ vs $S_{II}$) in the mixed-SPT regime.
paper_structure: The paper develops the measurement protocol, applies it to the MPS/dephasing model, analyzes the finite-size scaling of nonlinear correlators to pinpoint SW-SSB transitions, and complements this with string-order measurements to identify mixed-state SPT phases.
why_interesting: The methodology provides a concrete, experimental roadmap for probing complex, non-linear quantum phase transitions (like SW-SSB) in realistic, noisy quantum hardware, bridging quantum information diagnostics with condensed matter critical phenomena.
